thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU queue depth for 'gpu-pool-us-west-2' exceeded 5000, autoscaler attempted scale but saw repeated driver evictions and Xid errors. Scaling events blocked by NodeGroupCapacityExceeded and driver OOMs. Auto-created incident thread.

Jo (sre-oncall): seeing huge queue growth and 502s for inference requests.

Aisha (ml-oncall): logs show repeated 'CUDA Xid' errors and kernel panics on a subset of nodes, looks like memory corruption after long-running kernels.

Ravi (infra): autoscaler logs: "scale up failed: instance launch failed for 4/8 attempts - driver-installation-timeout". Also cloud reports some nodes were marked NotReady.

Marta (runtime): runtime traces show OOMs in driver -> GPUs getting evicted from kubelet. Effective GPU capacity dropped by ~40% in 7m.

Jo (sre-oncall): immediate action: pause admissions to Hosted API routes hitting the pool and enable fast-failover to Dedicated fallback. Can we toggle route fallback now?

Aisha (ml-oncall): yes I can flip fallback. Doing a config change:
```
redwood routes update --route /v1/generate --fallback dedicated:low-latency --drain-timeout 30s
```

Ravi (infra): can we bump autoscaler max nodes temporarily? policy currently max=50, we'll raise to 80 to allow room for replacement.

Marta (runtime): careful — driver instability may replicate to new nodes on rollout. Proposing: 1) cordon + drain nodes showing Xid errors, 2) disable driver autorestart, 3) rollout driver rollback to previous driver build.

Jo (sre-oncall): agreed. Steps:
- cordon/evict bad nodes
- scale up to 80
- rollback driver -> v1.9.3
- enable canary on subset of pool

Ravi (infra): scaling to 80 now (requested by Jo). Cloud logs indicate 20 new instances provisioning. Some failures remain due to node image bootstrap timeout.

Support (Customer Ops): We have 3 customers reporting timeouts; escalated to P1. Notifying affected customers with ETA ~30-60m.

Aisha (ml-oncall): rolling rollback in progress. Applying driver v1.9.3 to kube-daemonset.

Marta (runtime): monitoring KV-cache and runtime logs. Can we increase kubelet eviction threshold to be less aggressive while we stabilize?

Ravi (infra): increased kubelet eviction pressure thresholds on new nodes. Also reconfigured autoscaler backoff to be slightly less aggressive.

Jo (sre-oncall): traffic rerouted to dedicated fallback for high-latency routes. Queue is shrinking from 5k->1.2k in last 10m.

IncidentBot: NOTE: oncall handoff scheduled in 45m. Jo -> Aisha for long-tail mitigation.

Aisha (ml-oncall): takeover acknowledged. Will monitor driver OOM metrics and coordinate with runtime to run smoke tests before uncordoning.

Marta (runtime): smoke tests passed on 10 canary nodes. Uncordoning incremental batch.

Ravi (infra): new nodes now healthy. Autoscaler bumped back to normal max=50 after stabilization.

Jo (sre-oncall): system has recovered to 95% capacity. Keeping incident open for 2h to watch regressions. Filing postmortem.

Support (Customer Ops): sent update to affected customers: 'Mitigation in progress, degraded performance persists for some requests, routing fallback applied.'

Aisha (ml-oncall): root cause hypothesis: a recent driver build with subtle mem regression triggered OOM under our long-lived KV workloads. Postmortem will include reproduction and driver rollback checklist.

Jo (sre-oncall): handoff to Aisha now. I'm leaving the channel. :thumbsup:

Aisha (ml-oncall): taking over. Incident channel remains open. Adding action items: driver regression test, autoscaler backoff tuning, emergency capacity playbook.

IncidentBot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Duration so far: ~48m. Tags: gpu, autoscaler, driver, oncall-handoff.
